html:
The Tibetan Empire was a state centred on the Tibetan Plateau from the early 7th century to 842. At its height it reached from the Tang capital in the east to beyond Afghanistan in the west and down to the Bay of Bengal.

It began with Songtsen Gampo, the king of the Yarlung valley, who united the plateau and moved his capital to Lhasa. He married princesses from Nepal and Tang China, and the Jokhang temple was built to house the Buddha images they brought. The Tibetan script was created in his time, based on an Indian alphabet.

For two centuries Tibet was the great rival of the Tang along the Silk Road:

  • 670s: Tibet took the Tarim Basin cities from the Tang and beat a Tang army at Koko Nor in 678.
  • 763: after the An Lushan Rebellion weakened the Tang, Tibetan armies briefly occupied the capital Chang'an.
  • 821 to 822: a peace treaty fixed the border. Its text still stands on a pillar in Lhasa.

Under Trisong Detsen Buddhism became the faith of the court. Buddhism was made the state religion and the Samye Monastery was founded with teachers from India.

The empire broke apart after the death of King Langdarma in 842, in a fight over the succession. Tibet did not unite again for centuries, but the script, the Buddhist canon and the idea of a single Tibet all come from this time.
sum: The Tibetan Empire was a state centred on the Tibetan Plateau from the early 7th century to 842. At its height it reached from the Tang capital in the east to beyond Afghanistan in the west and down to the Bay of Bengal.
